h2: NDT training in the Southeast: radiography licensing, shipyard welding and terminal work
html:
NDT training in the Southeast: radiography licensing, shipyard welding and terminal work

NDT training for the Southeast follows one pattern across the region. Theory is self-paced and online. The practical is done on real parts at the employer's site, supported by the Practical NDT simulator. The employer then certifies the technician under its SNT-TC-1A written practice. What changes from state to state and sector to sector is the extra qualification the work demands, and radiography demands the most.

Radiography means a state license and radiographer certification. Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina and Tennessee are all NRC Agreement States. Across the Southeast, therefore, state radiation control programs license industrial radiography, not the NRC. Florida's guide shows what that involves. The Department of Health's Bureau of Radiation Control requires that:

  • radiographers are trained, tested and certified;
  • assistant radiographers work under a radiographer's personal supervision;
  • refresher training is given every year;
  • each radiographer's field performance is audited at least every six months.

An RT Level II course teaches the method. Radiation safety training and radiographer certification are separate steps that the employer, as the license holder, arranges.

Ship repair is adding welders, and weld inspection follows. A Small Shipyard Grant from the Maritime Administration, announced by the Transportation Secretary in Tampa in August 2026, is paying for a welder training program and new equipment at Gulf Marine Repair. More welding means more visual, magnetic particle and ultrasonic examination of the welds. For a yard trainee, a sensible order is visual testing and magnetic particle testing first. Ultrasonic testing comes next, for butt welds and hull gauging.

Fuel import and power plants. Florida has no refineries, and nearly half of its petroleum supply arrives through Port Tampa Bay. Tank and pipeline NDT in the state therefore centers on terminals: thickness surveys, tank floor scanning, and examination of repair welds. Gas-fired repowering adds boiler work. Tampa Electric's Big Bend station now runs two heat recovery steam generators. HRSG tube and header inspection draws on UT thickness and phased array skills, so a technician who wants power plant work should add PAUT after UT Level II.

Training through the storm season. The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June to November and can close coastal ports and plants at short notice. In 2024, Kinder Morgan's pipeline from Tampa to Orlando was shut for Hurricane Helene and shut again for Milton less than two weeks later. Online theory carries on through closures like these. The practical at the employer's site is scheduled around the employer's own recovery work, and enrollment is open all year, so a technician does not lose a training cycle to one storm.

Which course to start with.

  • Level I if you are new to NDT.
  • Level II if you already work under a Level II.
  • RT training if your employer holds a radiography license.
  • ASNT NDT Level III preparation once you have the experience ASNT requires.

Employers setting up a program can use the employer certification program under SNT-TC-1A. Florida technicians can also see NDT training in Florida and NDT training in Tampa. Tell us the methods, levels and state.
